newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SingTel sees pager sales dented from 1997.
newsitem.headline: SingTel sees pager sales dented from 1997.

text.p: Deregulation of Singapore's pager market in 1997 is likely to dent growth in sales in this sector for Singapore Telecommunications Ltd (SingTel), the company said on Friday.
Koh Boon Hwee, SingTel chairman, said he "expected some defection" to other service providers when the market was opened to free competition on January 1, 1997.
"There will be a dent in growth," he said.
Koh's comments came at a news conference to announce that SingTel's first-half net profit rose 13.6 percent to Singapore $843.5 million.

Revenue from mobile communciations operations, including paging, was up 21.5 percent at the half-year, with the bulk coming from increases in mobile phone and paging subscribers, said SingTel. Revenue from these operations formed 17 percent of group totals.
SingTel said its pager penetration covered 33.6 percent of the population.
Koh could not give an accurate estimate of how much market share the company expected to lose.
"The one thing we do know, is that we won't have a 100 percent market share," he said.
